chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to grant me wealth, so He granted me, and I asked Allah to grant me a son, so He granted me a son, and I asked Him to grant me a house, so He granted me, and I fear that this might be a gradual [leading to ruin].' So he said: 'By Allah, with praise, no.'

key_terms.اسْتِدْرَاجٌ: Gradual leading to ruin or disbelief by granting desires without spiritual growth
key_terms.مَعَ الْحَمْدِ: With praise/gratitude (indicating the condition for blessings not being a trap)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between divine blessing and istidrāj (gradual leading to ruin) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between *istidrāj* (gradual leading to ruin) and divine favor by emphasizing that the presence of gratitude (*hamd*) negates the fear of deception. This highlights a key Shia theological principle: blessings become a test of gratitude rather than a trap for the arrogant, provided the recipient maintains conscious thankfulness. The Imam’s emphatic 'Wa Allah' (By God) underscores the certainty of this condition for the common believer.
